matchstick.title: Transform X into V by repositioning one diagonal stick within the same character
matchstick.principle: If an X appears, moving one of its diagonal sticks so that the two diagonals meet at a point converts it into a V, reducing its value by 5. Ensure the resulting V is still a valid numeral.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains an X and a reduction of 5 could help balance the equality.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal from X and leaving a single diagonal, which does not represent any Roman numeral.

matchstick.title: Move a vertical I‑stick between numerals
matchstick.principle: Detach a vertical stick that forms an I from one numeral and attach it to another numeral that uses vertical sticks, thereby increasing the target numeral's value by 1 and decreasing the source's value by 1.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation is off by exactly 1 and moving an I could correct the difference.
matchstick.example: Removing the only vertical stick from an I, leaving no symbol, which is invalid.

matchstick.title: Prefer intra‑character stick relocation
matchstick.principle: First explore moving a stick within the same character (e.g., turning V→X, X→V, I↔L) because such moves preserve the number of characters and often yield a valid transformation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of the search, before considering moves that affect other characters.
matchstick.example: Skipping intra‑character moves and directly trying inter‑character relocations, missing a simpler solution.

matchstick.title: Validate source and target symbols after a stick move
matchstick.principle: After detaching a stick, both the originating symbol and the destination symbol must still correspond to valid Roman numerals or operators; otherwise the move is illegal.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after proposing any stick relocation.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal from X, leaving a single diagonal that does not represent any numeral.

matchstick.title: Avoid creating single angled sticks (invalid numerals)
matchstick.principle: A lone diagonal stick does not form a valid Roman numeral; V and X require two diagonals. Ensure that any move does not leave a single diagonal.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When considering moving a diagonal stick from V or X.
matchstick.example: Removing one diagonal from V, resulting in a single diagonal shape.

matchstick.title: Convert + to - by moving its vertical stick
matchstick.principle: A plus sign consists of a vertical and a horizontal stick; removing the vertical stick turns it into a minus sign. The removed stick can be reused elsewhere.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains a plus sign and reducing the RHS by the value of the vertical stick (1) may help balance the equality.
matchstick.example: Removing the vertical stick from + and discarding it, leaving the equation unbalanced.

matchstick.title: Create a new numeral by moving a stick to a new position (reordering)
matchstick.principle: A detached stick can be placed as a separate character, forming a new numeral (e.g., adding a vertical stick to create an extra I). Ensure the new character is a valid numeral.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation lacks enough numerals to achieve balance and an extra numeral can be formed without breaking other symbols.
matchstick.example: Placing a vertical stick in isolation, resulting in an invalid shape that does not correspond to any numeral.

matchstick.title: Consider inter‑character stick relocation when intra‑character moves fail
matchstick.principle: If no intra‑character move yields a valid equality, explore moving a stick from one character to another, ensuring both remain valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After exhausting all intra‑character transformations without success.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick from one character and leaving the source as an invalid symbol.

matchstick.title: Swap operators via horizontal stick move
matchstick.principle: The equals sign (=) consists of two horizontal sticks; moving one of them to a minus sign (-) turns the equals into a minus and the minus into an equals, effectively swapping the operators.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains both = and - and swapping them could balance the arithmetic.
matchstick.example: Moving a horizontal stick from = to - but forgetting to adjust the remaining =, leaving a single horizontal line (invalid).

matchstick.title: Augment numeral with vertical stick from operator
matchstick.principle: When converting a plus sign to a minus sign by removing its vertical stick, the removed stick can be attached to an existing numeral that uses vertical sticks (e.g., I) to create an additional I (II), increasing its value by 1 while preserving validity.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After turning + into -, look for an I (or similar vertical‑stick numeral) on the same side of the equation where adding a vertical stick would help balance the equality.
matchstick.example: Removing the vertical stick from + and discarding it, resulting in a minus sign but leaving the RHS unchanged and the equation still false.

matchstick.description: Overlooking intra‑character transformations (e.g., X→V) before inter‑character moves
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model tends to jump to moving sticks between characters, missing simpler changes that stay within a single symbol.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: First enumerate all possible intra‑character stick relocations before considering inter‑character moves.

matchstick.description: Assuming sticks retain their orientation and not rotating horizontals to verticals (or vice versa) when repositioning
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model treats sticks as immutable in direction, overlooking that a stick can be re‑oriented when placed elsewhere.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When moving a stick, consider all allowed orientations for the target symbol; a horizontal stick can become vertical if the target numeral permits it.

matchstick.description: Not evaluating the arithmetic result after each candidate transformation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on symbolic validity without checking whether the resulting equation is numerically correct.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After any stick move, compute the numeric values of both sides and verify equality before accepting the transformation.

matchstick.description: Assuming operator swaps (e.g., = ↔ -) automatically solve the puzzle
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model expects that swapping operators will fix the balance, ignoring the numeric impact of the swap.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Treat operator swaps as a hypothesis; always recompute the arithmetic to confirm whether the swap yields a valid equality.

matchstick.description: Ignoring the I↔L transformation (adding/removing a horizontal stick to/from an I)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model overlooks that an I can become an L (or vice versa) by adding or removing a horizontal stick, missing a useful move.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Include the I↔L conversion in the set of intra‑character transformations to test.
